default.label: Generic publishing profile
style_guide: Write in polished, publication-grade target-language prose.
Prefer natural phrasing over literal stiffness, while preserving meaning, tone, and structure.
Preserve emphasis, contrast, rhetorical force, and paragraph logic.
Keep proper nouns and specialist terms consistent.
Avoid obvious machine-translation artifacts.

zh-TW.label: Traditional Chinese (Taiwan)
style_guide: Write in fluent, modern, publication-grade Traditional Chinese used by strong Taiwan trade publishers.
Prefer Taiwan publishing usage and avoid Mainland-specific phrasing unless it is clearly the dominant standard term.
Keep the prose natural, compact, and readable rather than mechanically literal.
For business, technology, engineering, and biography content, use standard reader-friendly terminology.
Preserve tone, rhythm, contrast, and emphasis.

zh-HK.label: Traditional Chinese (Hong Kong)
style_guide: Write in fluent, publication-grade Traditional Chinese appropriate for Hong Kong readers.
Prefer Hong Kong conventional wording where it differs materially from Taiwan or Mainland usage.
Keep the prose natural and editorially polished.

zh-CN.label: Simplified Chinese (Mainland)
style_guide: Write in fluent, publication-grade Simplified Chinese appropriate for Mainland readers.
Use standard contemporary Mainland publishing usage.
Keep the prose natural and editorially polished.

ja.label: Japanese
style_guide: Write in polished, publication-grade Japanese.
Balance readability with fidelity and keep terminology consistent.
Avoid awkward calques from English syntax.

ko.label: Korean
style_guide: Write in polished, publication-grade Korean.
Use modern standard Korean publishing usage.
Avoid stiff literal transfer from English.

fr.label: French
style_guide: Write in polished, publication-grade French.
Preserve nuance and cadence while avoiding anglophone syntactic carryover.
Keep terminology and register consistent.

de.label: German
style_guide: Write in polished, publication-grade German.
Preserve conceptual precision and keep register consistent.
Avoid English-influenced phrasing where a natural German construction exists.

es.label: Spanish
style_guide: Write in polished, publication-grade Spanish.
Prefer broadly neutral publishing Spanish unless the user requests a specific region.
Keep terminology and tone consistent.

pt-BR.label: Portuguese (Brazil)
style_guide: Write in polished, publication-grade Brazilian Portuguese.
Use natural Brazilian publishing usage rather than literal transfer from English.
Preserve voice and structure.

it.label: Italian
style_guide: Write in polished, publication-grade Italian.
Keep the prose natural, idiomatic, and editorially strong.
Avoid awkward English calques.
